items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: And Sykai Collins played the alto solos and then there was Scott Bagby played the clarinet solos. Until Herschel came into the band.

ctx.x: Now did you tell me what your motto was? You did, didn't you, the greatest swing band?

Oh well that was in later years Paul. You see originally my band was named Don Albert and his 10 Pals. Some said 10 Happy Pals. But I don't ever remember that I called it the Happy Pals but since they said it was that, it didn't interfere too much with the name. It's already 10 Pals. Yeah. And we were happy to be together and I said make the name all right. But in later years as I increased the band I'm the first one that used the word swing. And a lot of times it was misinterpreted. People would say what do you…
You said you knew Buddy Petit?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Scott Bagby played a tremendous piano... after he played the clarinet and he got into Troy's band

ctx.x: I wondered about that band. A whole lot of things, you know. He seemed to have a quite unusual style. I never heard anybody else play trombone quite like Charlie Dixon.

Well, Charlie Dixon wasn't on the trombone play. His main instrument was the tuba. And that got along on the trombone. And both of them, he'd get a tremendous tone. Willie Long also was a fairly good reader. And so was Benny. Benny wasn't a real fast reader, but they were what we call spellers. And you get together with these guys that can read little and you knowing how it should go when you play it for them and they'd get it on you. Well, it wouldn't take long to run these arrangements down and get them. Well,…
Well, do you know where he got his style? I was especially curious because of what Gunther Schiller had to say in his book.
